questions.stem: Why can most organisms not use nitrogen gas (N2) directly from the atmosphere?

options.text: Because there is not enough nitrogen in the atmosphere
Because nitrogen is only found in the soil
Because the triple bond in N2 is very strong and difficult to break
Because nitrogen gas is poisonous

questions.explanation: Nitrogen gas (N2) has a very strong triple bond between the two nitrogen atoms, making it unreactive. Most organisms cannot break this bond, so they need nitrogen in more reactive forms like nitrates (NO3-) or ammonium (NH4+).

options.text: The absorption of nitrogen by animals
The conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia or nitrates
The breakdown of proteins into amino acids
The release of nitrogen gas into the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Nitrogen fixation is the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen gas (N2) into ammonia or nitrates that plants can absorb. This is carried out by nitrogen-fixing bacteria, some of which live in root nodules of leguminous plants.

questions.stem: Which type of bacteria converts ammonium into nitrates?

options.text: Nitrifying bacteria
Decomposing bacteria
Denitrifying bacteria
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria

questions.explanation: Nitrifying bacteria convert ammonium (NH4+) into nitrites and then nitrates (NO3-) through the process of nitrification. Nitrates are the main form of nitrogen that plants can absorb through their roots.

options.text: The absorption of nitrates by plant roots
The conversion of nitrates back into nitrogen gas
The conversion of nitrogen gas into nitrates
The breakdown of dead organisms

questions.explanation: Denitrification is the conversion of nitrates back into nitrogen gas by denitrifying bacteria. This process occurs in anaerobic (low oxygen) conditions, such as waterlogged soils, and returns nitrogen to the atmosphere.

questions.stem: Why is nitrogen important for living organisms?

options.text: It provides energy for photosynthesis
It is needed to make amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids
It is the main component of cell membranes
It is needed for respiration

questions.explanation: Nitrogen is essential for making amino acids (the building blocks of proteins), nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), and other important molecules like ATP and chlorophyll. Without nitrogen, organisms cannot grow or function properly.

questions.stem: Where are nitrogen-fixing bacteria found in leguminous plants?

options.text: In the leaves
In the flowers
In root nodules
In the seeds

questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (such as Rhizobium) live in root nodules of leguminous plants like peas, beans, and clover. This is a mutualistic relationship -- the bacteria fix nitrogen for the plant, and the plant provides the bacteria with sugars.

questions.stem: What is the role of decomposers in the nitrogen cycle?

options.text: They fix atmospheric nitrogen
They absorb nitrogen from the atmosphere
They break down dead organisms, releasing ammonium into the soil
They convert nitrates into nitrogen gas

questions.explanation: Decomposers break down proteins and other nitrogen-containing compounds in dead organisms and waste, releasing ammonium (NH4+) into the soil. This process is called ammonification and makes nitrogen available for nitrifying bacteria.
